description: The U.S. Drought Monitor is a weekly map of drought conditions across the United States that classifies areas into five intensity categories, from D0 abnormally dry through D1 moderate to D4 exceptional drought, with labels for short-term and long-term impacts. It is produced by the National Drought Mitigation Center at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln in partnership with the USDA, NOAA and NASA, with authors blending indicators and local reports. Coverage is the continental US, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and the US-affiliated Pacific islands and Virgin Islands, with weekly maps since 2000 released every Thursday at 8:30 Eastern Time using data up to the previous Tuesday. GIS files, county and state statistics by category, time series and maps in PNG, PDF and TIF formats can be downloaded free; reuse terms are on a permission page that the page read does not detail. Caveats: the map is an expert synthesis, not a single measured index, so category boundaries reflect judgement and change with revisions of method. For simulation it gives weekly drought hazard layers and county exposure statistics for agricultural losses, water supply stress and cooling-water risks to power plants, and for climate adaptation analyses. It is related to the Census of Agriculture record in this catalogue, which gives the farm exposure in the same counties.
